key_insight: An exact worst-case theory identifies a unique, monotonically decreasing minimax-optimal SGD stepsize schedule when the noise variance bound is sufficiently large.
engineering_relevance: The results provide principled stepsize guidance for smooth convex stochastic optimization and rule out minimax gains from fixed fractal schedules in the stated regime.
method: Analyze expected final-iterate suboptimality under conditionally zero-mean gradient noise with bounded variance.
Cover any N-step schedule in [0, 1.5]^N for problem dimensions d ≥ N + 1.
Construct matching objectives and noise distributions, then derive the optimal schedule.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports matching worst-case constructions rather than empirical benchmarks, with optimality and uniqueness when the variance bound is at least Ω(1/√N).
watch_item: The guarantees concern smooth convex problems under specific noise, dimension, and stepsize assumptions; they do not establish performance for nonconvex training.
paper_title: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization
